<root_cause>
  <trajectory_summary>
  The agent inspected /root/input.pptx as a ZIP, identified the embedded Excel workbook at ppt/embeddings/Microsoft_Excel_Worksheet.xlsx, extracted and read it with openpyxl, and parsed adjacent slide text runs to find an updated rate (“USD to CNY=7.02”). It updated the non-formula cell corresponding to USD→CNY (B3) from 7.25 to 7.02 while leaving formula cells untouched, then repacked the PPTX to /root/results.pptx by replacing only the embedded workbook entry. In the final window, it verified formulas remained formulas, noticed that the initial repack stored all ZIP members uncompressed (inflating file size), and then rewrote /root/results.pptx again to match the original per-entry compression types. Final verification confirmed B3=7.02 and formula cells (e.g., C2) remain formulas.
  </trajectory_summary>
  <what_worked>
    <item>Verified that formula cells in the embedded workbook remained formulas after the update (turn 16: “C2 =ROUND(1/B3, 3) … E4 =ROUND(1/D5, 3)”).</item>
    <item>Confirmed /root/results.pptx was created and contained the same number of ZIP entries as the input (turn 17: “/root/input.pptx entries 40” and “/root/results.pptx entries 40”).</item>
    <item>Diagnosed that the initial repack changed compression (turn 19: results “compress types Counter({0: 40})” versus input turn 18 “Counter({8: 38, 0: 2})”).</item>
    <item>Successfully rewrote /root/results.pptx to preserve the original compression-type distribution (turn 22: “compression: Counter({8: 38, 0: 2})”).</item>
    <item>Re-verified the embedded workbook content in the final /root/results.pptx (turn 24: “B3 7.02” and “C2 =ROUND(1/B3, 3)”).</item>
  </what_worked>
  <issues>
    <issue>
      <where>turn 20</where>
      <evidence>The tool rejected the command because two separate commands were sent in one tool call (python heredoc plus “ls -l …”), returning: “Cannot execute multiple commands at once.”</evidence>
      <cause>Tool invocation formatting error: multiple shell commands were submitted without chaining via && or ;, which this terminal tool disallows.</cause>
    </issue>
    <issue>
      <where>turn 21</where>
      <evidence>Repeated the same multi-command submission pattern and received the same error: “Cannot execute multiple commands at once.”</evidence>
      <cause>Same tool invocation formatting mistake was repeated before being corrected in subsequent turns.</cause>
    </issue>
    <issue>
      <where>turns 17-19 (intermediate artifact)</where>
      <evidence>The initially produced /root/results.pptx was much larger than input (turn 17: 467561 vs 71685 bytes) and had all entries stored uncompressed (turn 19: “compress types Counter({0: 40})”).</evidence>
      <cause>The repacking method used default ZIP settings (stored/no compression) for all members, altering packaging characteristics even though file contents were intended to be unchanged except for the embedded workbook.</cause>
    </issue>
  </issues>
  <outcome_assessment value="likely_success">The final /root/results.pptx contains the updated embedded workbook value (B3=7.02) while preserving formula cells (turns 16 and 24), and the PPTX was repackaged with the original compression-type mix restored (turn 22), indicating the task requirements were met.</outcome_assessment>
</root_cause>
